args.brief: An interactive rhythm game for phones: neon title screen, buttons, a toggle and a slider for options, four lanes of notes on the beat of synthesized music, a score, results with a rank and a replay button.

args.name: clip-12-tap-the-beat
args.title: Tap the beat
args.description: An interactive clip: a neon rhythm game played in the browser from a share link. Title, a 12-bar song on four lanes (tap or D F J K), results with a rank and play again.

args.name: ui-dialog
args.note: the scrim is a modal region: what is under it takes no focus or hotkeys

args.name: ui-button
args.note: The one thing to do next. A primary button at the bottom of a vertical scene (width 100 in a safe box 0.9 wide, size 12: a thumb-sized target), a secondary and a ghost under it with delay 0.08 and 0.16. Pitfall: keep outDur 0 when the scene holds for input (the playhead waits on the scene's last frame, so an exit would leave it half faded); a label that cannot fit its box at the 2.6 % floor throws instead of shrinking. Works: { "label": "Start", "icon": "arrow-right", "hotkey": "Enter" }; disabled bound to a boolean while a dialog is open. Pair with ui-tx-iris (the next scene opens from the tap on it) and ui-dialog.

args.name: ui-toggle
args.note: Settings rows (sound, vibration, hints). The whole row is the target and change carries the new boolean: { "set": { "sound": "$value" } } (or { "toggle": "sound" }). Pitfall: without a bound `on` it emits but never moves. Works: three rows in safe boxes 0.92 x 0.11, 0.125 apart, a detail line on the ones that need it, delay 0.06 apart; plate false over a plain backdrop in a wide frame. Pair with ui-slider in the same settings scene and a ghost ui-button "Done" to leave it.

args.name: ui-slider
args.note: Volume, speed, difficulty, a guess on a scale. The track is a range region: dragging and the arrow keys (after Tab) both emit change with the value snapped to step. Pitfall: bind value, or the thumb stays where it was; display "auto" shows a percentage for a 0 to 1 range with no prefix, suffix or decimals, the value otherwise. Works: { "label": "Speed", "min": 0.5, "max": 2, "step": 0.25, "decimals": 2, "suffix": "×" } (ticks show for 2 to 12 steps). Pair with ui-toggle in a settings scene; send it pulse to point at it in a tutorial.

args.name: ui-score
args.note: Scores, lives, coins and countdowns in a HUD. Bind value and add to the variable from the wires: the number ticks, pops, flashes (red on a loss) and floats the difference. Pitfall: the pop and the floating "+10" reach outside the item's box, so leave room around it; the stack style uses the display face (Anton), whose digits are not tabular, so place it centred. Works: a pill { "label": "Score", "icon": "star" } top right (safe 0.8, 0.07, 0.38 x 0.1), a plain { "icon": "heart", "color": "#ff5c8a" } for lives top left, a stack with size 14 on a results screen. Pair with ui-progress and ui-toast.

args.name: ui-toast
args.note: Feedback that comes and goes: send it success, error or show with the text as the value from any wire (show takes a tone prefix: "ok: …", "error: …", "info: …", "warn: …"). Pitfall: it draws nothing until an event arrives (blank in stills and the thumbnail) unless text is set; a message longer than two lines at the floor throws, so keep it short. Works: one toast item for the whole timeline, edge "top", hold 1.8, success "Correct, +10" and "error: Not quite" from the answer wires; text with hold 0 for a status line in a video. Pair with ui-card reveals, ui-score and ui-button presses.

args.name: ui-dialog
args.note: Confirmations and modal news (leave the game? level complete): Enter confirms, Escape cancels, a tap on the scrim cancels (or is swallowed with scrimTap "block"), and nothing under it takes a tap. Pitfall: an item shown with `when` keeps its scene's time, so send it open as it appears to replay the entrance, or bind open and leave `when` out (then it also animates out); give it the whole frame as its box, on the top track. Works: tone "danger" with icon "trash-2" for a destructive choice; one button (cancel "") with tone "success" and icon "trophy" for good news. Pair with disabled bound to the same variable on the controls under it, and ui-toast after a confirm.

args.name: ui-tx-iris
args.note: Opening the next scene from what was tapped: the pressed button seems to swell into the next screen, edged by a glowing ring in the theme's accent. Pitfall: after a key or a timer the pointer is the last one (or none), so set origin "center" or a point for those wires; in a video it always opens from x, y. Works: duration 0.6 to 0.7 on the go action of a Play button low in the frame. Pair with ui-button and ui-card (pick a card, open its scene).

args.name: beat-lanes
args.note: A whole rhythm game in one asset: give it the same bpm as a music-loop starting with it and wire perfect/good/miss to a score. The event value is the lane, so a wire can set a variable from it and play a sound per lane. Caught notes are worked out from f.ui (a region that fired after the note came into reach), so replays are exact. Bind speed to a slider (0.6 to 1.6) and showKeys to a toggle.

args.name: beat-title
args.note: A title screen that stays alive while an interactive scene holds (it moves on f.ui.now). Keep the title above the sun: at size 26 on a vertical frame use sun 15 and horizon 0.615; with title and subtitle empty it is a backdrop (the results scene of clip 12).

args.name: beat-results
args.note: Bind score, hits, perfects and best to the game variables and give total the number of notes; the rank and stars come from hits/total. Leave the lower quarter for ui-button items (play again, menu).

args.name: theme-neon
args.note: For games and night-time energy. Adds accent4 (amber) to the usual theme shape; assets that know only three accents mix one.

args.name: beat-lanes
args.note: cheaper to draw: one fill per area (no full-frame gradient, one radial glow, fewer glow passes)
